mainTopic: תוספת on holy days and eating on ערב יום כיפור; which foods and drinks count as eating and drinking on יום הכפורים
overview: This amud opens at the end of רב פפא's source: יום הכיפורים itself is called 'שבת', so a שבת-type warning applies to it. The גמרא asks why רב אחא בר יעקב did not use that verse. It answers that he needs it for a ברייתא that teaches תוספת, adding weekday time onto holy days at the start and the end, for יום הכיפורים, ימים טובים and שבתות. The תנא of 'עצם' 'עצם' uses 'בתשעה' for חייא בר רב מדפתי's teaching: eating on the ninth counts as if one fasted on both the ninth and the tenth. The גמרא then returns to the משנה's rule about food that is not fit to eat. רבא says chewing pepper or ginger is פטור, and challenges from ערלה and from a ברכה are answered by splitting moist from dry. A ברייתא teaches that reed leaves are not food but young grapevine shoots are, and two אמוראים define how young the shoots must be. Finally, the משנה's ruling on fish brine implies that vinegar is a drink, following רבי. When רב גידל ruled against רבי, people drank diluted vinegar on יום הכפורים, and he explained that his ruling was far narrower.

steps.title: רב פפא: יום הכיפורים itself is called שבת
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא finishes his source: יום הכיפורים itself is called 'שבת' in the פסוק 'תשבתו שבתכם'.
steps.simpleTranslation: יום הכיפורים itself is called 'שבת,' as it is written: 'You shall rest on your שבת.'
steps.whatsHappening: We are joining the end of רב פפא's answer. He says the Torah calls יום הכיפורים itself 'שבת', so the rules of a שבת apply to it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, the גמרא was looking for a source for the אזהרה (warning) on יום הכיפורים. רב פפא does not borrow from another passage. He points to a verse about יום הכיפורים itself, where the day is called 'שבתכם'.

keyTerms.meaning: you shall rest on your Shabbat (ויקרא כג:לב)

phrases.english: It itself (Yom Kippur) is called 'Shabbat,'
as it is written: 'You shall rest on your Shabbat.'

steps.triggerLanguage: הוּא גּוּפֵיהּ שַׁבָּת אִיקְּרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רב פפא's derivation, which began on the previous amud.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: יום הכיפורים is itself called 'שבת' by the Torah, so it carries a שבת-type אזהרה.

steps.title: Why didn't רב אחא בר יעקב use רב פפא's verse?
steps.stepSummary: We understand why רב פפא prefers his own source. But why didn't רב אחא בר יעקב use רב פפא's verse?
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense that רב פפא did not say like רב אחא בר יעקב, because a verse written about the matter itself is better. But רב אחא בר יעקב — why didn't he say like רב פפא?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא compares the two opinions. It explains one side easily, then asks about the other side. This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא's verse speaks directly about יום הכיפורים. That is stronger than learning it from somewhere else, as רב אחא בר יעקב did. So the real puzzle is why רב אחא בר יעקב would skip such a direct verse.
steps.confusionAlert: This is not an attack on רב פפא. The 'בשלמא' half defends רב פפא. The question is only about רב אחא בר יעקב.

phrases.english: Granted, Rav Pappa

phrases.aramaic: לָא אָמַר כְּרַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב —
phrases.english: did not say like Rav Acha bar Yaakov —
because a verse written about the matter itself is preferable.
But Rav Acha bar Yaakov,

phrases.aramaic: מַאי טַעְמָא לָא אָמַר כְּרַב פָּפָּא?
phrases.english: what is the reason he did not say like Rav Pappa?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא רַב פָּפָּא לָא אָמַר כְּרַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Compares רב פפא's source from step 1 with רב אחא בר יעקב's earlier source.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why רב אחא בר יעקב does not use the verse 'תשבתו שבתכם' as his source.

steps.title: He needs the verse for adding time onto יום הכיפורים
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר יעקב needs this verse for a ברייתא. Reading 'בתשעה' together with 'בערב' teaches that the fast starts while it is still day, on the ninth. This is תוספת.
steps.simpleTranslation: He needs it for what was taught in a ברייתא: 'And you shall afflict your souls on the ninth of the month.' Could it mean one starts fasting during the day of the ninth? The verse says 'at evening.' If 'at evening,' could it mean once it gets dark? The verse says 'on the ninth.' How so? One starts fasting while it is still day. From here we learn that we add from the weekday onto the holy day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers step 2. רב אחא בר יעקב needs this פסוק for another lesson: we must add some weekday time before יום הכיפורים starts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse gives two clues that seem to clash. 'On the ninth' suggests daytime, but 'at evening' suggests nightfall. Putting them together gives late afternoon of the ninth, just before dark. Starting the fast then means adding חול time onto the קודש day.

keyTerms.meaning: he needs it (for a different teaching)
as was taught in a ברייתא
the verse teaches / therefore it says
we add from the weekday onto the holy day (תוספת)

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the classic source for תוספת יום הכיפורים: we stop eating before sunset on ערב יום כיפור.

phrases.english: He needs it for that which was taught in a Baraita:
'And you shall afflict your souls on the ninth of the month.'
One might think he should start fasting during the ninth —
therefore the verse says: 'at evening.'
If 'at evening' — one might think only once it gets dark?
Therefore the verse says: 'on the ninth.'
How so?
He begins fasting while it is still day,
from here we learn that we add from the weekday onto the holy.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ לְכִדְתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The verse is needed for a different teaching (מיבעי ליה).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the verse is so direct, it seemed every אמורא should use it as the source for the אזהרה.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב אחא בר יעקב uses this verse for the law of תוספת, so he needs a different source for the אזהרה.

steps.title: Adding time extends to the end of the day, יום טוב, and שבת
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues. 'מערב עד ערב' adds time at the end of the day, 'תשבתו' extends תוספת to ימים טובים, and 'שבתכם' extends it to שבתות.
steps.simpleTranslation: I only know this for its beginning; from where do I know it for its end? The verse says: 'from evening until evening.' I only know this for יום הכיפורים; from where for ימים טובים? The verse says: 'you shall rest.' I only know ימים טובים; from where for שבתות? The verse says: 'your שבת.' How so? Every place 'rest' (שבות) is stated, we add from the weekday onto the holy.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא keeps going and widens the rule of תוספת. It goes step by step: the end of יום הכיפורים, then ימים טובים, then שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each new word of the פסוק adds a new case. 'מערב עד ערב' makes the end match the beginning, so we add time at both ends. 'תשבתו' and 'שבתכם' extend the rule to every day called a day of rest (שבות). The result is a general rule for all of them.

keyTerms.meaning: I only know (from the verse so far)

steps.whatToRemember: תוספת applies at the beginning and the end of the day. It applies to יום הכיפורים, ימים טובים, and שבת — wherever the Torah says 'rest.'
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for adding time before and after שבת and יום טוב, as in accepting שבת early and ending it late.

phrases.english: And I only know this at its entry;
at its exit, from where do we know?
The verse says: 'from evening until evening.'
And I only know Yom Kippur;
Festivals, from where?
The verse says: 'you shall rest.'
I only know Festivals;
Shabbatot, from where?
The verse says: 'your Shabbat.'
How so?
Every place where 'rest' is said,
(from here) we add from the weekday onto the holy.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵין לִי אֶלָּא בִּכְנִיסָתוֹ, בִּיצִיאָתוֹ מִנַּיִן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא from step 3 and widens its rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Weekday time is added at both the start and end of יום הכיפורים, ימים טובים, and שבתות.

steps.title: What does the תנא of 'עצם' 'עצם' learn from 'בתשעה'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא turns to the תנא who learns from 'עצם' 'עצם' and asks how he uses the phrase 'בתשעה לחודש'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the תנא who learns from 'עצם' 'עצם' — what does he do with this phrase 'on the ninth of the month'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks about another opinion: a תנא who learns his source from the repeated word 'עצם'. It asks what that תנא learns from 'בתשעה לחודש'. This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא assumes every phrase in the פסוק must teach something. So for this תנא too, it asks what 'בתשעה לחודש' teaches.

keyTerms.meaning: 'that same' day — a word repeated in the פרשה and used for a comparison
what does he do with it? (how does he use the verse)

phrases.english: And the Tanna of 'etzem'-'etzem,'
this phrase 'on the ninth of the month' —
what does he do with it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתַנָּא דְּ״עֶצֶם״ ״עֶצֶם״, הַאי ״בְּתִשְׁעָה לַחוֹדֶשׁ״ מַאי עָבֵיד לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from רב אחא בר יעקב to the תנא of 'עצם' 'עצם', asking about the same phrase used in step 3.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the תנא of 'עצם' 'עצם' learns from the phrase 'בתשעה לחודש'.

steps.title: Eating on the ninth counts like fasting
steps.stepSummary: He uses it for חייא בר רב מדפתי's teaching. The Torah says 'בתשעה' to teach that eating on the ninth counts as if one fasted on the ninth and the tenth.
steps.simpleTranslation: He needs it for what חייא בר רב מדפתי taught. חייא בר רב מדפתי taught: 'And you shall afflict your souls on the ninth' — do we fast on the ninth? Don't we fast on the tenth! Rather, it tells you: anyone who eats and drinks on the ninth, the verse credits him as if he fasted on the ninth and the tenth.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers step 5. This תנא uses 'בתשעה' for a different lesson: eating on ערב יום כיפור is like fasting.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חייא בר רב מדפתי notices a problem: the fast is on the tenth, so why does the פסוק mention the ninth? He explains that the Torah links the ninth to the 'affliction.' Eating on the ninth is credited as a fast, so it is as if one fasted two days.

keyTerms.meaning: but is it really so that…? (rhetorical question)

steps.whatToRemember: There is a מצוה to eat on ערב יום כיפור. It is credited as if one fasted on both the ninth and the tenth.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the well-known source for the מצוה of eating and drinking on ערב יום כיפור.
steps.confusionAlert: 'וכי בתשעה מתענין' is not a challenge to the halacha. It is חייא בר רב's own rhetorical question, used to set up his teaching.

phrases.english: He needs it for that which was taught by
Chiya bar Rav of Difti.
As Chiya bar Rav of Difti taught:
'And you shall afflict your souls on the ninth' —
but do we fast on the ninth?
Don't we fast on the tenth!
Rather, it comes to tell you:
anyone who eats and drinks on the ninth,
the verse credits him
as if he fasted on the ninth and the tenth.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ לְכִדְתָנֵי חִיָּיא בַּר רַב מִדִּיפְתִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The תנא of 'עצם' 'עצם' uses 'בתשעה' to teach that eating on the ninth counts as fasting on the ninth and the tenth.

steps.title: Chewing pepper or ginger on יום הכפורים is exempt
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's case of eating food that is not fit to eat. רבא gives two examples: chewing pepper or ginger on יום הכפורים is פטור.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'If he ate food that is not fit for eating' he is exempt. רבא said: Someone who chews peppers on יום הכפורים is exempt. Someone who chews ginger on יום הכפורים is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line in the משנה about eating things that are not real food. רבא gives two practical examples of this rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The prohibition of eating on יום הכפורים only covers real food. רבא says pepper and ginger are not considered food, so chewing them is not 'eating' and there is no כרת. These examples set up the challenges that follow.

keyTerms.meaning: Foods that are not fit for eating

steps.confusionAlert: פטור here means he is not liable to כרת or a קרבן, because this is not halachic 'eating.' It does not automatically mean it is fully permitted to chew pepper on יום הכפורים.

phrases.english: [The משנה said:] If he ate food that is not fit for eating.
phrases.notes: A quote from the משנה, opening a new topic

phrases.english: רבא said:
If one chews peppers on יום הכפורים, he is exempt.
If one chews ginger on יום הכפורים, he is exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: כַּס פִּלְפְּלֵי בְּיוֹמָא דְכִפּוּרֵי — פָּטוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the משנה. It is not connected to the previous discussion about תוספת and eating on the ninth.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Chewing pepper or ginger on יום הכפורים is not considered eating, so one is פטור.

steps.title: Challenge from רבי מאיר: pepper is a food tree for ערלה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא in which רבי מאיר learns from 'עץ מאכל' that pepper is a food tree and is subject to ערלה. That suggests pepper is food, which goes against רבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged this. רבי מאיר used to say: From the fact that the verse says 'you shall count its fruit as ערלה,' don't I already know it is a food tree? So why does the verse say 'עץ מאכל'? It means a tree whose wood and fruit taste the same, and that is pepper. This teaches that pepper is subject to ערלה. And ארץ ישראל lacks nothing, as it says, 'You will not lack anything in it.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבא with a ברייתא that seems to treat pepper as real food.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר says the extra words 'עץ מאכל' include pepper, a tree whose wood is as edible as its fruit. ערלה only applies to food trees. So if pepper is subject to ערלה, it is called 'food,' and then chewing it on יום הכפורים should count as eating.

keyTerms.meaning: They challenged (introduces a challenge from a ברייתא)
Fruit of a tree in its first three years, which is forbidden
Why does the verse need to say this?
You must say (this is the only option left)

steps.whyThisMatters: The ברייתא adds a side praise: ארץ ישראל is so complete that even pepper grows there.

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
phrases.notes: This is how the גמרא brings a challenge from a ברייתא.

phrases.english: רבי מאיר used to say:
From what is implied by what is stated:
'And you shall count its fruit as ערלה,'
don't I know that it is a food tree?!
phrases.notes: The word 'fruit' already shows it is a food tree

phrases.english: So why does the verse say 'a food tree'?
It means a tree whose wood and fruit taste the same.
You must say this is pepper,
to teach you that pepper is subject to ערלה.
And ארץ ישראל lacks nothing,
as it says: 'You will not lack anything in it'!

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵיתִיבִי, הָיָה רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the first half of רבא's statement, the part about pepper.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's ruling that chewing pepper on יום הכפורים is פטור
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Pepper is subject to ערלה, which applies only to food trees. So pepper is food, and chewing it should count as eating.

steps.title: Moist pepper versus dry pepper
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא is talking about fresh, moist pepper, which is food. רבא is talking about dry pepper, which is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. This one, the ברייתא, is talking about moist pepper. That one, רבא, is talking about dry pepper.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the challenge by showing that the two sources are talking about different kinds of pepper.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Fresh, moist pepper is edible, so it counts as food for ערלה. Dry pepper is too sharp to eat on its own, so it is not food, and chewing it on יום הכפורים is not eating. Both sources are correct, each about its own case.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult (the two sources do not contradict)

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
This one (the ברייתא) is about moist pepper,
and that one (רבא) is about dry pepper.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא: הָא — בְּרַטִּיבְתָּא, וְהָא — בְּיַבִּישְׁתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from רבי מאיר's ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא): moist versus dry
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Pepper is either always food or never food.
steps.terutzMaskana: Moist pepper is food (subject to ערלה). Dry pepper is not food (chewing it on יום הכפורים is פטור).

steps.title: Challenge from רב נחמן: ginger gets a ברכה
steps.stepSummary: רבינא challenges מרימר with רב נחמן's ruling. Ginger from India is permitted, and one says בורא פרי האדמה on it. That suggests ginger is food, which goes against רבא's ginger example.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said to מרימר: But didn't רב נחמן say that this ginger coming from India is permitted, and we say the ברכה 'בורא פרי האדמה' on it?
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא challenges the second half of רבא's statement, the part about ginger.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן treats Indian ginger as permitted food, with no worry about בישולי גוים, and requires a ברכה on it. A ברכה and a food prohibition only make sense for real food. So ginger seems to be food, and chewing it on יום הכפורים should count as eating.

keyTerms.meaning: A type of ginger (preserved or cooked)
The ברכה on produce that grows from the ground

phrases.english: רבינא said to מרימר:
But didn't רב נחמן say:

phrases.aramaic: הַאי הִימְלְתָא דְּאָתֵי מִבֵּי הִנְדּוּאֵי — שַׁרְיָא,
phrases.english: This ginger that comes from India is permitted,
and we recite over it the ברכה 'Who creates the fruit of the ground.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבִינָא לְמָרִימָר: וְהָאָמַר רַב נַחְמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the pepper challenge was answered, this is a parallel challenge to רבא's ginger example.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's ruling that chewing ginger on יום הכפורים is פטור
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Ginger gets a ברכה of בורא פרי האדמה and is treated as permitted food. So it is food, and chewing it should count as eating.

steps.title: Moist ginger versus dry ginger
steps.stepSummary: The same answer is given. רב נחמן is talking about moist ginger, which is food. רבא is talking about dry ginger, which is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. This one, רב נחמן, is talking about moist ginger. That one, רבא, is talking about dry ginger.
steps.whatsHappening: The challenge about ginger is answered the same way as the challenge about pepper.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Moist ginger is edible, so it gets a ברכה and is treated as food. Dry ginger is not normally eaten, so chewing it on יום הכפורים is not eating. רבא's two examples are both about the dry form.
steps.whatToRemember: Pepper and ginger are food only when fresh and moist. Dry pepper or ginger is not food, so chewing it on יום הכפורים is פטור.

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
This one (רב נחמן) is about moist ginger,
and that one (רבא) is about dry ginger.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא: הָא בְּרַטִּיבְתָּא, וְהָא בְּיַבִּישְׁתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבינא's challenge, using the same distinction as step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא): moist versus dry
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Ginger that gets a ברכה must always count as food.
steps.terutzMaskana: Moist ginger is food and gets a ברכה. Dry ginger is not food, so chewing it on יום הכפורים is פטור.

steps.title: Reed leaves are not food, but grapevine shoots are
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that eating reed leaves on יום הכפורים is פטור, but eating grapevine shoots is חייב.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: If someone ate reed leaves, he is exempt. If he ate grapevine shoots, he is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with two more examples of what counts as food on יום הכפורים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Reed leaves are not something people eat, so eating them is not real 'eating' and one is פטור. Young grapevine shoots are soft and edible, so they count as food and one is חייב.

keyTerms.meaning: Liable (here, to כרת or a קרבן)

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
If one ate leaves of reeds, he is exempt.
If he ate grapevine shoots, he is liable.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the theme from step 7 of food that is or is not fit to eat, with new examples.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Reed leaves are not food (פטור). Grapevine shoots are food (חייב).

steps.title: Which grapevine shoots count as food?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what exactly the ברייתא means by 'grapevine shoots'.
steps.simpleTranslation: What are these grapevine shoots?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a clarifying question about the ברייתא. This sets up the next step, where two אמוראים answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Grapevine shoots harden as they get older and become wood. So the גמרא needs to define which shoots are still soft enough to be food.

keyTerms.meaning: Which are these? (asks for a definition)

phrases.english: Which are these grapevine shoots?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵלּוּ הֵן לוּלְבֵי גְפָנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for a definition of a term in the ברייתא of step 12.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How young must a grapevine shoot be to count as food?

steps.title: Two opinions on how young the shoots must be
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק מגדלאה says shoots that sprouted between ראש השנה and יום הכפורים. רב כהנא says shoots from the last thirty days.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק מגדלאה said: All shoots that sprouted from ראש השנה until יום הכפורים. And רב כהנא said: All shoots from thirty days.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים answer the question and give different time limits for which shoots are still food.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both agree that only fresh, soft shoots count. רבי יצחק מגדלאה allows about ten days (from ראש השנה). רב כהנא allows a longer window of thirty days before יום הכפורים.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak from Migdal said:
All that sprouted from Rosh HaShanah
until Yom Kippur.
And Rav Kahana said:
All that sprouted within thirty days.
phrases.notes: Meaning thirty days before יום הכפורים.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק מִגְדְּלָאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 13 with two opinions.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יצחק מגדלאה: shoots from ראש השנה to יום הכפורים. רב כהנא: shoots from the last thirty days.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports רבי יצחק מגדלאה
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא repeats the same law and defines grapevine shoots exactly like רבי יצחק מגדלאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא like רבי יצחק מגדלאה: If one ate reed leaves, he is exempt. If he ate grapevine shoots, he is liable. Which are grapevine shoots? All that sprouted from ראש השנה until יום הכפורים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that matches רבי יצחק מגדלאה's view word for word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first part of this ברייתא is the same as step 12. What is new is the definition at the end, which supports רבי יצחק מגדלאה over רב כהנא.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא in agreement with him

steps.whyThisMatters: A ברייתא backing one אמורא gives his view more weight, so the shorter window from ראש השנה is the stronger position.

phrases.english: It was taught in accordance with Rabbi Yitzchak from Migdal:
If one ate reed leaves, he is exempt,
and if grapevine shoots, he is liable.
Which are grapevine shoots?
All that sprouted from Rosh HaShanah
until Yom Kippur.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא כְּווֹתֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יִצְחָק מִגְדְּלָאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the first opinion of step 14.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יצחק מגדלאה's definition: shoots that sprouted between ראש השנה and יום הכפורים.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that gives the same definition.

steps.title: Fish brine is exempt, so vinegar must be liable
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה that drinking fish brine is פטור and infers that drinking vinegar is חייב.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: If one drank fish brine or fish-pickling liquid, he is exempt. This implies that if he drank vinegar, he is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line of the משנה about drinks and makes an inference from what the משנה left out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lists only brine as 'not a drink' and does not list vinegar. So the גמרא infers that vinegar is a real drink and makes one חייב.

keyTerms.meaning: Briny liquid used to pickle fish

phrases.english: If one drank fish brine or pickling liquid, he is exempt.
This implies that for vinegar, he is liable.
phrases.notes: We learn this because the משנה didn't list vinegar with the drinks he's exempt for.

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁתָה צִיר אוֹ מוּרְיָיס — פָּטוּר. הָא חוֹמֶץ — חַיָּיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: New topic: from foods to drinks in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Brine is not a drink (פטור). By inference, vinegar is a drink (חייב).

steps.title: Whose view is the משנה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא holds that vinegar counts as a drink.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view is our משנה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks who the author of the משנה is. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Calling vinegar a real drink is not obvious, since vinegar is sharp. So the גמרא wants to find the תנא who holds this.

phrases.english: Whose view is our Mishnah?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִיתִין מַנִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks who stands behind the inference of step 16.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא holds that vinegar is a drink?

steps.title: The משנה follows רבי: vinegar revives the spirit
steps.stepSummary: The משנה follows רבי, who says in a ברייתא that vinegar refreshes a person, so it counts as a drink.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is רבי. As it was taught: רבי says: Vinegar revives the spirit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the משנה follows רבי and quotes a ברייתא as proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since vinegar refreshes a thirsty person, רבי treats it as a real drink. So drinking it on יום הכפורים makes one חייב.

keyTerms.meaning: רבי יהודה הנשיא, editor of the משנה

phrases.english: It is Rabbi.
As it was taught: Rabbi says:
Vinegar revives the spirit.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי הִיא. דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 17.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה follows רבי, who holds that vinegar revives the spirit and is a drink.

steps.title: רב גידל rules against רבי
steps.stepSummary: רב גידל בר מנשה taught publicly that the הלכה does not follow רבי about vinegar.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב גידל בר מנשה from Birei DeNeresh taught publicly: The הלכה is not like רבי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a story. רב גידל rules publicly that vinegar is not a drink for this purpose.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Ruling against רבי means drinking vinegar on יום הכפורים does not bring the full punishment. The next steps show how people misread this ruling.

phrases.english: Rav Giddel bar Menashe taught publicly
from Birei DeNeresh:
The halacha is not like Rabbi.

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּרֵשׁ רַב גִּידֵּל בַּר מְנַשֶּׁה מִבֵּירֵי דְנַרֶשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a practical ruling against the view identified in step 18.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הלכה is not like רבי. Vinegar does not make one חייב on יום הכפורים.

steps.title: People drink diluted vinegar the next year
steps.stepSummary: The next year, everyone mixed vinegar with water and drank it on יום הכפורים.
steps.simpleTranslation: The next year everyone went out, mixed vinegar with water, and drank it.
steps.whatsHappening: The story continues. The people took רב גידל's ruling as permission to drink vinegar on יום הכפורים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The public heard 'not liable' and understood 'allowed'. This sets up רב גידל's reaction in the next step.

phrases.english: The next year everyone went out
mixed and drank vinegar.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְשָׁנָה נָפְקִי כּוּלֵּי עָלְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows how the public acted on the ruling of step 19.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The public treated the ruling as permission to drink diluted vinegar.

steps.title: רב גידל explains his ruling was much narrower
steps.stepSummary: רב גידל gets angry and explains three limits: he meant only after the fact, only a small amount, and only undiluted vinegar.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב גידל heard and became angry. He said: I said it only after the fact. Did I say it is allowed from the start? I said it about a little. Did I say a lot? I said it about pure vinegar. Did I say diluted?
steps.whatsHappening: רב גידל rejects how the people understood him. He shows that his ruling was limited in three ways.
steps.deeperAnalysis: First, 'not liable' never means 'allowed to begin with'. Second, he spoke about a small amount, not a full drink. Third, he spoke about harsh pure vinegar, while diluted vinegar is pleasant and is a real drink.

keyTerms.meaning: From the start, as the proper way

steps.whatToRemember: פטור does not mean מותר. רב גידל's ruling covered only a small amount of pure vinegar, after the fact. Drinking diluted vinegar on יום הכפורים is clearly forbidden.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think diluted vinegar is more lenient because it is weaker. It is the opposite. Pure vinegar is too harsh to be a normal drink. Diluted vinegar is pleasant and drinkable, so it is a real drink.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a classic lesson that a public ruling of פטור can easily be misread as permission. That is why פטור אבל אסור matters so much.

phrases.english: Rav Giddel heard and became angry.
He said: Say that I said it after the fact,
did I say it from the start?
Say that I said it about a little,
did I say it about a lot?
Say that I said it about pure vinegar,
did I say it about diluted vinegar?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵימַר דַּאֲמַרִי אֲנָא — דִּיעֲבַד, לְכַתְּחִלָּה מִי אֲמַרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the public's reading (step 20) of the ruling in step 19.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the public's broad reading of רב גידל's ruling, not the ruling itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: They confused 'not liable' with 'permitted', a small amount with a lot, and pure vinegar with diluted vinegar.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Vinegar is forbidden on יום הכפורים. רב גידל's leniency covers only a small amount of pure vinegar, after the fact.
